summary: Penor 02 both studied under and taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Dilgo Khyentse, Jampel Gyepai Dorje, and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo. In 1978, he founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Gustaf John Ramstedt at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1939), where he served as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh, later serving as lecturer there (1982–1989) and as professor at Leipzig University (1994–2017).

Per Kværne (born 1945) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Oslo (~1965–1973). He lectured at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as professor at the University of Oslo (1975–2007).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1968–1972) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1973–1991).

Perry Link (born 1944) works in Sinology and linguistics. After earning a B.A. from Harvard University (~1962–1966), he held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Munich (~1976–1996), he held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson (born 1972) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1995–2001), later holding posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).
Peter Alan Roberts specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under Michael Aris.

Peter Bisschop specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Leiden University (attested 2011–2021).

Peter Connolly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later directing the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.
Peter Fenner specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist who studied at Regensburg, Mainz (PhD 1952), and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003; visiting professor 1972).
Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics (-1990) and held an adjunct post at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).
Peter Haskel works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) earned his PhD at Yale University (~1957–1961). He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1965–1970), Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).
